name: Reinhold Pussycat
approach: Reach the East Creek basin by climbing the Bugaboo Snowpatch Col to the upper Vowell Glacier, crossing toward the Pigeon-Howser Col and descending to the East Creek Glacier. The East Creek bivy is on a rib of rock and scree, a short way below the Minaret. From camp, go directly uphill to the west face's left side. name: East Buttress of the South Peak
approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Above Daiphy Lake,

name: North Ridge
approach: Reach it over the Sphinx Glacier by the Castle Towers approach, or paddle the lake to Sphinx Bay and climb from there. Then go up the glacier to the foot of the north ridge. The lower pitches are blocky scrambling, and the proper climbing begins higher up, on cracks that split the slab.
overview: A fine route up the North Ridge in six pitches. P1 and P2 are blocky scrambling (5.3, 5.5), and P1 is comfortable to solo for most. P3 and P4 follow numerous slab cracks (5.7) that all open into chimneys under a big horizontal break; belay by slingin
path: The Sphinx < Garibaldi Park < Sea to Sky (Squamish to Whistler) < British Columbia

name: Northeast Ridge

Follow it as far as the junction signed for Granite Park and Honeymoon Lake, go around Honeymoon Lake, and continue up the drainage. Leave the trail and travel cross-country to a camp near Golden Lake. The route starts left of the toe of the northeast ridge, left of an orange right-facing corner.
descent: Descend the west slope of the peak and return through Royce Col.

Take the dirt road to a single-track, then climb the hillside well east of Horse Creek, following game trails and use trails on the east side of Blacksmith Creek. There is no maintained trail, so expect casual sidehilling and some thick brush. Pass the cliffs and talus fields, then cross to the west side of the creek where it enters a canyon,

Either way, you reach the Vogelsang High Sierra Camp at the foot of the peak. Take the trail from the camp toward Vogelsang Lake. About halfway up, the trail passes close to a big slab on the west side of the peak broken by many vertical cracks; the buttress above that slab is where the route climbs.

name: Choose Joy

Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby

name: Bigger than Life
approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. This route is on Mega Dome, uphill and southeast of base camp, and takes the crack and ramp system left of the huge roof on the dome's north face.
descent: After the last pitch, belay on the slabs above, walk the ridge east and rappel from slings on the north side of the dome.

It starts on the northwest arete of the shark-fin dome that sits above and south of Mega Dome.

name: Stone Meysan

A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. The route is the third crack from the left on the north face, reached from the ledges below the corner.

name: North face
approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. The route follows a prominent crack system near the centre of the face.
path: North Face, The < Mt. Hoffman < May Lake Area < Tuolumne Meadows

name: Public Enemy Number One
approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. It is the leftmost crack on the north face; get to it by traversing in from the left, or by one of several easy-angled lines up from the boulder-strewn ledges.
descent: Walk down to climber's left, or continue up the northeast ridge.
overview: Reach the leftmost crack from a traverse coming in on the left, or by scrambling up gentle options from the boulder-strewn ledges, and follow the crack. For the descent, walk off to the left, or carry on up the NE Ridge.
path: North Face, The < Mt. Hoffman < May Lake Area < Tuolumne Meadows

name: Shelob
approach: From May Lake, work up the slabs and round toward the northeast side of the summit, then drop into the clear valley that heads toward the north face. A steep snowfield guards the base and needs snow-travel experience; the wall sees few ascents and loose rock is common. Start on a ledge that a small chasm separates from the main wall, a short way below and left of a small pine; the line goes up the centre of the face.
descent: From the plateau, hike southeast and drop down the second- and third-class talus and slabs of the northeast face.

path: North Face, The < Mt. Hoffman < May Lake Area < Tuolumne Meadows

name: Fingers and Blades
approach: The crag is on the reservoir shore and is easiest by boat or kayak from the launch, which has day parking; it can also be reached on foot from near the dam. The route is at the crag's north end, beside a class 4 gully, and starts from a good ledge up a thin to mid-width crack.
overview: Start from a good ledge on an obvious thin-to-medium crack, which continues to a tiny finger crack. A cedar tree beside the crack, on its right, can be slung. The other cracks nearby make good top-rope lines.
path: On The Water < Spicer Reservoir < Bear Valley < Ebbets Pass Highway (4)

name: Angels and Demons
approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Angels and Demons climbs the middle buttress, down and left of Friends; look for the pillar with a rappel anchor and the flake crack to its left.
descent: Scramble off, or rappel the route: every belay is bolted, and the first rappel runs from the second anchor straight down to a pedestal and then the ground.
overview: A strong line up the central of three buttresses, on high-quality rock, though a few cracks are somewhat vegetated. Grades stay at 5.10 or below apart from the short roof on P2. Every belay has bolts, and one 70m rope handles the rappel: from the P2

name: Spring Roll
approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Spring Roll takes the leftmost of the three formations, starting at its toe up a right-facing layback corner.

name: Tendernob
approach: Tendernob lies deep in the Gorge of Despair country and takes a backpack trip. The usual way in starts on Highway 180 about a mile west of Cedar Grove, climbs by the Lewis Creek trail (or the Deer Cove trail) to Frypan Meadow, then takes the west branch up to the end of the trail above Grizzly Lake. name: Broken Arrow
approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, skirt the right shore and scramble up directly beneath the long fracture that runs up to the base of Arrowhead, then work diagonally left up grassy ledges into the cirque and continue up and right for the routes above the lake. The route starts in the middle of the large grassy ledge, between Arrowplane and Warhead, and trends up the ramp system to the left of Warhead.
descent: After topping out on Lost Arrowhead or Warhead, walk down to the cairned saddle on the west side, rappel a couple of times, and downclimb back to the base of the wall where gear was left.
overview: Four pitches flanked by Arrowhead and Warhead, roughly parallel to Warhead on its left up its own ramp system. P1 (150'): from the grassy ledge about 40 ft to Warhead's left, weave up slab rated 5.8 PG-13 with intermittent cracks, then blocky ground
path: Arrowhead < Glacier Gorge < Rocky Mountain National Park < Colorado

name: Orange Pillar
approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge lot (or take the shuttle) and follow the trail toward Black Lake by way of Mills Lake. At Black Lake, skirt the right shore and scramble up beneath the long fracture that leads to the base of Arrowhead, then angle left up grassy ledges into the cirque. The line sits on the left portion of the face, between the upper ramp that leads to the summit and the ledge used for access, immediately left of several dihedrals that run the whole height.
